exposure: ultrasound guidance for caudal epidural steroid injections
anatomical variations of sacrum and sacral hiatus (mean distance between bilateral sacral cornua, mean distance between anterior and posterior wall of sacral hiatus apex)
outcome: success of caudal epidural injections (visualisation of needle in sacral hiatus, turbulence of injected contrast agent in sacral canal, correct placement of needle and filling of epidural space with contrast agent via fluoroscopy)
cohort: 32 adult patients (16 male and 16 female) with low back pain who were scheduled for caudal epidural steroid injections.
finding: Ultrasound guidance proved to be a safe and reliable modality for observing anatomic variations of the sacral hiatus and performing caudal epidural injections, achieving success in 31 out of 32 patients.
